messages:
ava_cs: Hey team, escalation from a mid-size SaaS customer — they saw duplicate full generations after an SSE disconnect + reconnect. Reported two full completions (and double billing) within ~3s of each other. App: notes-streamer-prod. Customer says they reconnected immediately when they saw a partial final chunk. :grimacing:

sam_eng: ugh. do we have their session ids / last_event_id? any idempotency-key in the request?

ava_cs: Copied from their support dump (sanitized):

```
POST /v1/stream HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.com
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx
Idempotency-Key: (none)
Last-Event-ID: evt_1732
Session-Token: sess_9f2c
Client: notes-web-1.4.2
```

They said client reconnected by opening a fresh SSE and did not replay any payload. Client logs show immediate reconnect after 'connection reset'.

priya_support: They attached a client-side trace: reconnect happened ~1.2s after the last partial chunk. Server sent a small partial chunk, then a reconnect, then we sent another full completion. They were billed for both. Customer is requesting a refund but wants root cause too.

sam_eng: Can you paste the last few server-side events (if we logged them) for that session token? Also which model?

ava_cs: Model is rw-medium-compat (hosted). I grabbed partial server log snippet: 

```
[2026-03-10T14:21:33.112Z] sess_9f2c chunk seq=7 partial=true
[2026-03-10T14:21:34.320Z] connection reset from client sess_9f2c
[2026-03-10T14:21:35.450Z] new stream opened no idempotency header; assigned stream_id=s_881
[2026-03-10T14:21:35.452Z] resume check: last_ack=seq=6; client reported last_event_id=evt_1732 -> mismatch
[2026-03-10T14:21:35.460Z] serving generation gen_555 (full) -> tokens 0..n -> emitted
```

devon_infra: Looks like resume semantics didn't line up — client reported last_event_id but server's last_ack points elsewhere -> server accepted new stream and started a brand new generation while not suppressing re-emit of final chunk. If client didn't include an idempotency key the server can't safely dedupe at the generation level.

sam_eng: Two problems combined: (1) resume token mismatch -> fallback to new generation; (2) no idempotency-key per logical request -> duplicates billed. We should still avoid re-sending the same final output when reconnects are within a short grace window.

priya_support: Customer says their client didn't intentionally replay; they expected resume to pick up. They want fix + billing credit.

ava_cs: For immediate mitigation I offered: 1) grant credit for the duplicate invoice line for that session, 2) advise client to include an idempotency-key per user operation, 3) recommend exponential backoff on immediate reconnects for streaming (small delay to allow server to reconcile). Customer accepted the credits if we confirm root cause.

sam_eng: Repro plan (small dev repro):
1) open SSE, start generation -> server emits partial chunk and pauses
2) force client TCP reset
3) immediately open new SSE with same session-token but no idempotency-key and last_event_id set to previous chunk id (simulate mismatch)
4) observe server behavior: does it start a new generation or resume; check billing audit logs for two generation records

devon_infra: I'll spin up a local repro on staging and capture both the resume decision path and billing write. Hypothesis: we do a quick fallback to new generation when last_event_id != server last_ack; but we don't mark the previous generation as 'suppressed' for billing. If within 5s we should treat as 'likely duplicate' and mark billing suppressed if generation is identical — but we don't today.

sam_eng: Short-term server patch options: A) when resume mismatch and a new generation is started within a small window (<3s) for the same session-token+client, attach a transient dedupe-id based on KV-cache of last-output-hash and suppress billing if output-hash matches previous generation. B) require/encourage idempotency-key and return clearer guidance in client docs. Option A is safer for customers but riskier from implementation complexity.

priya_support: Customer needs final ETA so we can reply. Can we do quick staging repro + temporary billing credit today?

devon_infra: I can run staging repro in ~90m and validate whether the output hash matches. If confirmed we can issue a manual billing reversal for that invoice line; finance ok with manual credit once we confirm duplicate generation id.

sam_eng: I'll draft a small PR to add a 3s transient dedupe check on the resume path and a monitoring flag. If devon confirms the repro we can roll to canary tonight. I can't promise tomorrow but will try for today if the repro is trivial.

ava_cs: Great. I'll reply to customer: we acknowledge duplicate generation caused by resume mismatch + missing idempotency-key; we will refund the duplicate and follow up with a fix plan + recommended client-side improvements.

deploy-bot: [notice] ticket #CS-4789 attached to thread; staging job started by devon_infra (job-id: sj-9921).

priya_support: Thanks — tagging @sam_eng and @devon_infra for follow-up. I'll hold the refund until you confirm the staging result so we have notes for billing.

sam_eng: acked. keeping thread updated with repro output + diff of billing entries.

ava_cs: thanks all. closing loop with the customer once devon posts staging logs. :thumbsup:
